caseno: Appeal from Original Order No. 25 of 1983.
lawyer:
SC Das ----- For the Appellant. 
M Fazlul Karim with Amirul Karim Chowdhury ----- For the Respondent.
parties:
Bhakti Bhusan Shaha ----- Appellant
Vs.
Moulana Ruhul Amin ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
Md Abdul Jalil J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 8-6-83 passed by the District Judge, Chittagong in Misc. Case No. 49/83 rejecting an application filed u/s. 25 of the Guardians and Wards Act. 

 2. The appellant Bhakti Bhusan Shaha filed an application u/s. 5 of the Guardians and Wards Act in the court of the District judge, Chittagong alleging that his minor son Ganesh Chandra Shaha who appeared in the SSC Examination, while residing in the hostel of the Collegiate School, respondent opposite party No. 3, Abdus Sattar Khondker, the Superintendent of the School Hostel along with OP 1 Moulana Ruhul Amin and OP 2 Moulana Shamsuddin removed Ganesh therefrom in 1982 by taking recourse to inducement, fraud and undue influence. For the welfare of Ganesh he is required to be returned to the custody of his father the petitioner and so be prayed for causing his son Ganesh to be arrested and delivered into the custody of the petitioner-appellant. The said application was numbered as Misc. Case No. 49/83 and opposite party No. 1 contested the said case by filing a written objection denying the material allegations and stating, in substance, that for welfare and interest of the minor he should not be delivered to the custody of his parents and that said Ganesh embraced Islam of his own free will voluntarily by denouncing the Hindu religion on 11-8-83 and changed his name to Md. Omar Farooq. It was further alleged that Mr Omar Farooq @ Ganesh was aged 18 years. 

 3. The said Md Omar Farooq @ Ganesh also filed a written objection stating that he is not a minor but his age was wrongly recorded in the admit card and the school certificate and that he was not willing to go with his father. Md Omar Farooq @ Ganesh was examined on oath before the court. The petitioner was examined as PW 1 who in his deposition substantiated the case made out in his application. Md. Omar Farooq @ Ganesh in his examination-in-chief stated. 

 6. Section 25 of the Guardians & Wards Act, 1890 reads as follows:— 

 "Title of Guardian to custody of Ward—(1) If a ward leaves or is removed from the custody of a guardian of his person, the court, if it is of opinion that it will be for the welfare of the ward to return to the custody of his guardian, may make an order for his return, and for the purpose of enforcing the order may cause the ward to be arrested and to be delivered into the custody of the guardian. 

 (2) For the purpose of arresting the ward, the Court may exercise the power conferred on a Magistrate of the first class by section 10 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (V of 1898). 

 7. Mr M Fazlul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent submits that the learned District Judge rightly passed the order considering the welfare of the minor. In support of his contention lie cited the case of Sarat Chandra Chakraborty vs Forman and another, reported in ILR 12 Allahabad 1213 wherein it was held by a Division. Bench of the Allahabad High Court that a minor Hindu over the age of 16, who had embraced Christianity and left the house of his elder brother by whom he had been maintained and brought up, appeared to be well able to take care of and provide for himself, and preferred to be left as he was and had sufficient mental capacity to judge what was best for himself and the Court refused to make any order upon an application by the brother for his custody and guardianship. Mr Karim also cited the case of Rahimannessa & another vs Ashraf Mia and others, reported in 25 DLR 167 wherein it was also held that the paramount consideration is such cases is the welfare of the minor. We are also of the view, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, that it will not be proper to return Omar Farooque to the custody of his father in view of the fact that he is now a Muslim of his own free will and his father is a Hindu and be maintains himself. We called both father and son and permitted them to talk to each other freely in a separate room and we also talked to them. We are informed by the appellant's son that he will not go with his father and shall remain Muslim and his father also says that he will not allow his son to remain a Muslim and shall not take him back as a Muslim. We have already observed that the boy is trying to prosecute his higher studies in the Chittagong University and that he earns enough by working a private tutor. The boy appears to be able to take care of and provide for himself and has sufficient mental capacity to judge what would be for his best interest for his welfare. Therefore, he should be allowed to remain as he is.
